title: McKinsey 7S Framework
subtitle: You've made a strategic shift new direction, new structure, new hires but results aren't
useWhen: following. Something is misaligned but you can't identify what. The strategy is clear but the execution keeps resisting it.
howToUse: Developed by McKinsey consultants Tom Peters and Robert Waterman in 1980, the 7S Framework maps seven interdependent elements of an organisation that must all be aligned for strategy to work. The Hard Ss - Strategy (plan), Structure (org chart), Systems (processes and IT) are the visible elements. The Soft Ss - Shared Values (culture and beliefs), Skills (capabilities), Style (leadership approach), Staff (people) - are invisible but often more powerful. When any element is misaligned with the others, change stalls. AI can run a 7S diagnostic on your business and identify where the friction lives.
steps: Run a 7S audit whenever a strategy, restructure, or major change is not producing expected results.
Shared Values sits at the centre of the model, it is the element that all others must align to.
Changing one S always affects others, map the cascade before acting.

Use the output to prioritise: fix the most misaligned S before addressing the others. Diagnose why change isn't sticking and what to fix first Fixing Structure or Systems can happen in a quarter. Shifting Shared Values or Style takes years, not months. If your 7S audit says culture is the misalignment, don't expect the same timeline you'd use for an org chart change. The Soft Ss Take Longer
origin: Tom Peters & Robert Waterman, McKinsey & Company — 7S Framework, 1980
promptBody:
Act as a McKinsey organisational consultant using the 7S Framework.
My company               :  [DESCRIBE YOUR BUSINESS, STAGE, RECENT CHANGES]
The strategy I am trying to execute: [WHAT YOU WANT TO ACHIEVE]
What is not working :  [WHERE EXECUTION IS STALLING]
Diagnose all 7 elements for my organisation:
STRATEGY            :  The plan, is it clear and understood?
STRUCTURE         :  How are we organised,  does it serve the strategy?
SYSTEMS              :  Processes, tools  do they enable or block?
SHARED VALUES :  Culture - does it support or resist the change?
SKILLS                   :  Do we have the capability we need?
STYLE                     :  Does leadership behaviour match the strategy?
STAFF                     :  Do we have the right people in the right roles?
Identify the 2 most misaligned Ss.
Recommend the sequence to address them with a suggested timeframe for each step.

proTip:
The most common 7S misalignment is between Strategy and Shared Values. Leadership
changes direction but the culture hasn't moved  and culture always wins. If your strategy
requires behaviours that your current culture punishes or ignores, fix the culture
alignment before investing more in the strategy.
